EnvironmentCapabilities.ExpectedOutcome: Resolved data-root inis/PCSX2.ini exists, is non-empty, parses, and contains the default USB1/USB2/JVS sections -- created by the emulator's own -testconfig mechanism, never hand-authored by TPM.

Trigger.Description: The title's own .acgame archive carries a [data] jvsmode key. When jvsmode=lightgun, VMManager.cpp unconditionally sets USB1/USB2 Type=guncon2 and calls ACJV::SetMode(JVS_MODE::LIGHTGUN) -- TPM has no role in triggering this and must not attempt to.

RuntimeCapabilities.ExpectedOutcome: Post-launch evidence confirms the emulator itself reached JVS_MODE::LIGHTGUN with Type=guncon2 on both USB ports for this title. Evidence source not yet resolved -- see experiments.md for the pending controlled-launch experiment that must confirm which signal (log line, persisted ini state, or neither) is actually reliable before this capability can advance past Investigating.

EvidenceReferences.Description: EmuFolders::GetPortableModePath() reads portable.txt content; empty content defaults to the literal subfolder name "TeknoParrot" (fork-specific customization, source comment: "Default to TeknoParrot subfolder so all data stays organised under the exe directory"). Non-empty content is used as the literal data-root subfolder name instead.

-testconfig is a purpose-built headless init path: main() returns EXIT_SUCCESS immediately after InitializeConfig(), before any window or event loop. InitializeConfig() calls Save() synchronously when the ini does not already exist.

USB::GetConfigSection(port) returns "USB{port+1}" (sections [USB1]/[USB2]); USB::GetConfigString's real key is fmt::format("{}_{}", devname, key), i.e. guncon2_cursor_path for the guncon2 device -- not [USB Port N guncon2] / cursor_path.

GunCon2Device::UpdateSettings() reads cursor_path but unconditionally clears it in memory when ACJV::GetMode() == JVS_MODE::LIGHTGUN (source comment: "In TP LIGHTGUN mode our OSD overlay draws the crosshair; suppress guncon2's own PNG cursor"). Not yet confirmed whether a TPM-written cursor_path value on disk is harmless-but-inert or actively misleading to inspect post-launch.

When a title's .acgame [data] jvsmode field equals "lightgun", VMManager.cpp unconditionally calls Host::SetBaseStringSettingValue("USB1"/"USB2", "Type", "guncon2") and ACJV::SetMode(JVS_MODE::LIGHTGUN), and logs "ACGAME: jvsmode=lightgun -> GunCon2 on USB1+USB2" via Console.WriteLn. Whether this log line reaches a file under <DataRoot>/logs, and whether the Type write survives to disk after a clean shutdown, are both unconfirmed -- see experiments.md.

Ran pcsx2-qtx64.exe -testconfig -portable against isolated scratch copies (no live arcade data touched): exit code 0 in all runs; no UI window observed; first run 1774ms creating the full TeknoParrot\ tree; second identical run 227ms with a byte-identical ini SHA-256 (confirms idempotent, IsDirty()-gated save); empty portable.txt produced TeknoParrot\inis\PCSX2.ini; portable.txt="CustomDataRoot" produced CustomDataRoot\inis\PCSX2.ini with no TeknoParrot\ folder at all.

The certified arcade machine's live pcsx2x6\TeknoParrot\inis\PCSX2.ini has [USB1]/[USB2] sections (both Type = None at time of observation) and a separate top-level [JVS] section; it has no [USB Port N guncon2] section anywhere, confirming the real on-disk contract matches ev-usb-ini-contract, not TPM's prior assumption.

The certified cabinet's own GameProfiles\*.xml carry <GunGame>true</GunGame> on every current EmulatorType=pcsx2x6 title (cobrata, cobrataw, timecrs3, timecrs4, vnight) and it is absent on non-gun pcsx2x6 titles checked (acedriv3, tekken4, soulclb2) -- the field this contract's RuntimeCapability ApplicabilityPredicate keys on.

Crosshair PNG deployment to <Pcsx2Dir>\TeknoParrot\crosshairs\ (vs. the legacy <Pcsx2Dir> root) is a file-placement concern from issue #79, independent of the ini/JVS findings above, and the same deployment code path also serves ElfLdr2/standard game folders that this investigation did not examine. Retained as TPM-owned pending separate evidence on whether it still matters for pcsx2x6 specifically.

DriftPolicy.RevalidationTrigger: Recheck when the installed build's window-title version string no longer matches MatchedCommitMap, or when PS2Homebrew-arcade/pcsx2x6's default branch HEAD moves past the pinned commit and TPM is updated to track it.
